prompt: What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?
answer:
The algorithm is **block sort**—also known through implementations such as **WikiSort** and **GrailSort**.

It is:

- **Stable**
- **In-place** (typically \(O(1)\) auxiliary memory)
- **Worst case:** \(O(n\log n)\)
- **Best case:** \(O(n)\), for already sorted or nearly sorted input

**Timsort** also has \(O(n)\) best-case and \(O(n\log n)\) worst-case time, but it generally requires \(O(n)\) auxiliary memory, so it is not strictly in-place.
